mechanism_narrative: The recent drop in WORKPLACES mobility, combined with weak TRANSIT and flat RETAIL_REC, signals fewer weekday trips into commercial areas. If this pattern persists, retail and recreation visits will stay below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its last 28-day mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover from their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in GROCERY_PHARM indicates household trips are being redirected to essential errands rather than discretionary outings. That substitution suppresses retail and recreation mobility in the following one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0% after being positive in the prior three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining near zero or negative after its recent decline.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility spikes while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed, leisure demand is concentrated in open-air local trips instead of shopping districts. That pattern predicts lower retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 20% while TRANSIT stays below -10% and WORKPLACES stays below -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days when PARKS remains elevated and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises while TRANSIT falls further, the share of activity occurring at home increases and discretionary shopping trips are displaced. This home-consolidation mechanism lowers retail and recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases above 3% while TRANSIT drops below -15%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next 7 days after a simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and deeper fall in TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained positive PARKS mobility implies weather-supported outdoor activity and shorter indoor shopping time. That seasonal outdoor substitution should depress retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while PARKS remains above its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT together with a less negative WORKPLACES trend signals renewed commuting. More commuting expands incidental shopping opportunities, lifting retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES rises by at least 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after concurrent increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM normalizes toward zero after staying positive, households are exhausting essential trip demand and reallocating time back to discretionary outings. That transition should raise retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM moves from above 5% to between -2% and +2%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM returning to near-baseline levels.

mechanism_narrative: A combined rise in RESIDENTIAL and fall in WORKPLACES indicates stronger stay-at-home behavior, which directly suppresses discretionary retail trips. The effect should appear quickly and persist for about a month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL is above 2% and WORKPLACES is below -25% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES stays deeply negative.
